description: Delegated-scope map for duty1g/x64dbg-mcp-server (71 tools). Every tool is placed. Unmapped tool names are denied (unmappedPolicy=deny). This file is the reviewable authorization artifact; the proxy loads it, it is not hardcoded. A tool entry may be a scope string, a deny object, or an object {scope, args} where args declares per-argument constraints (argument-level policy).
argumentPolicyNote: Tool-name scope decides WHICH tools a credential may call; the optional per-tool `args` object decides HOW MUCH within a granted tool. Matchers: required, enum, max/min (numeric, accepts 0x-hex), maxLength, prefixOneOf, pattern, denyPattern. Evaluation is fail-closed. Examples below: ReadMemory caps size to 4096 bytes per call so a read scope cannot bulk-extract; DumpMemory/DumpModule confine the output path to a sandbox prefix and reject traversal.
classificationPrinciples: read is strictly non-mutating: it observes process/debugger state and returns data. Nothing that changes state (including analysis-DB annotations or clearing logs) is read.
control changes execution flow and breakpoint state but does not write process memory/registers or move bytes to disk.
write mutates process memory, registers, thread run-state, patches, or the debugger's persistent analysis database (comments, labels, bookmarks, event log).
session controls the debug target's lifecycle (load/attach/stop/restart). These create or destroy the thing every other scope operates on.
exfil moves process memory to disk. It is separated from read because a read scope must not authorize bulk extraction to the filesystem.
A tool whose capability cannot be bounded from outside the process (arbitrary command or expression surface) is denied or flagged, never silently mapped to a scope.

scopes.x64dbg:read: Observe process and debugger state. Non-mutating.
scopes.x64dbg:control: Drive execution and breakpoints (run, step, pause, breakpoints, thread switch).
scopes.x64dbg:write: Mutate process memory, registers, thread run-state, patches, or the debugger analysis database.
scopes.x64dbg:session: Create or destroy the debug target (load, attach, stop, restart).
scopes.x64dbg:exfil: Write process memory to disk (memory/module dumps).

ExecuteDebuggerCommand.reason: Arbitrary x64dbg command string. Reaches the capability of most of the other 70 tools, so any scope mapping would be a bypass. Denied outright. See ADR-0001.

EvalExpression.caveat: SECONDARY CATCH-ALL RISK. x64dbg's expression engine is broader than a pure reader: depending on build it can dereference and, in some contexts, assign. It is mapped to read for analyst usefulness but is a documented residual. Operators wanting a hard boundary should move it to deny here (it is config, not code). See ADR-0001 and README threat model.
